title: A geometric criterion for Kuga–Satake algebraicity
exact_target: Let (S,h) be a primitively amply polarized projective complex K3 surface. Put $V=h\perp $ in $H^{2}(S,Q)$, with its primitive quadratic Hodge structure, and assume $Hg(V)=SO(V,q)$, so $T(S)=V$. Are the following three conditions equivalent? First, some rational codimension-two correspondence from S to a complex abelian variety acts nontrivially on V. Second, there is a smooth connected projective surface Y and a dominant generically finite morphism $f:Y\to S$ such that tracing the wedge products of holomorphic one-forms on Y to $H^{0}(S,\Omega ^{2}_S)$ gives a nonzero map. Third, for every specified standard full Kuga–Satake Clifford, polarization and realization datum, a rational codimension-two cycle induces the prescribed Kuga–Satake map on $T(S)=V$.
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
\paragraph{Statement recorded in the supplied source.}
Let (S,h) be a primitively amply polarized projective complex K3 surface. Put $V=h\perp $ in $H^{2}(S,Q)$, with its primitive quadratic Hodge structure, and assume $Hg(V)=SO(V,q)$, so $T(S)=V$. Are the following three conditions equivalent? First, some rational codimension-two correspondence from S to a complex abelian variety acts nontrivially on V. Second, there is a smooth connected projective surface Y and a dominant generically finite morphism $f:Y\to S$ such that tracing the wedge products of holomorphic one-forms on Y to $H^{0}(S,\Omega ^{2}_S)$ gives a nonzero map. Third, for every specified standard full Kuga–Satake Clifford, polarization and realization datum, a rational codimension-two cycle induces the prescribed Kuga–Satake map on $T(S)=V$.

\subsection{Short English statement}
Let (S,h) be a primitively amply polarized projective complex K3 surface. Put $V=h\perp $ in $H^{2}(S,Q)$, with its primitive quadratic Hodge structure, and assume $Hg(V)=SO(V,q)$, so $T(S)=V$. Are the following three conditions equivalent? First, some rational codimension-two correspondence from S to a complex abelian variety acts nontrivially on V. Second, there is a smooth connected projective surface Y and a dominant generically finite morphism $f:Y\to S$ such that tracing the wedge products of holomorphic one-forms on Y to $H^{0}(S,\Omega ^{2}_S)$ gives a nonzero map. Third, for every specified standard full Kuga–Satake Clifford, polarization and realization datum, a rational codimension-two cycle induces the prescribed Kuga–Satake map on $T(S)=V$.
